quotes.text: Music was always a part of my life growing up. My family was very musical, and we would often sing and perform together. I knew from a young age that I wanted to make music my career.

I always put a lot of time and effort into preparing for my shows. I would work on my choreography, my vocals, and my overall performance for months before going on tour. I wanted to make sure that every aspect of the show was perfect for my fans.
I was always looking for new and creative ways to express myself through my music. I would draw inspiration from everything around me, whether it was other musicians, films, or even everyday life.

I would practice for hours and experiment with different dance moves until I found something that felt right. The moonwalk was actually a move that I had been working on for a long time before I ever performed it on stage.

As an artist, I believe it is important to use my platform to address issues that affect people's lives. I wanted to use my music to bring attention to these issues and to inspire people to take action and make a positive change in the world.

I always wanted my videos to be more than just a visual accompaniment to the song. I wanted them to be a work of art in their own right. I would work closely with the director and the production team to come up with a concept that would bring the song to life in a visually stunning way.

I think my music has influenced other musicians in many ways. My unique style and sound has inspired countless artists to create their own music, and my performances have set the bar for what a truly great live show should be.
Creating Thriller was a long and challenging process, but it was also one of the most rewarding experiences of my life. To see the album become such a huge success was truly a dream come true.
I always wanted my music to be inclusive and bring people together. I think the key to connecting with such a wide audience was to create music that was both relatable and universal.

Creating my music videos was a collaborative process. I would work with the director and the production team to come up with a concept, and then we would spend weeks or even months designing the sets and costumes. It was always a lot of hard work, but it was also a lot of fun.

I think my music resonates with people because it speaks to universal emotions and experiences. Love, heartbreak, joy, and sadness are all emotions that people can relate to, regardless of their age or background.
